## Seat review (`domain:services`) — content verified independently, docs-drift row checked and clear

### The load-bearing claim, re-derived from source rather than accepted

This PR's whole justification for needing no maintainer ruling is *"nothing accepts or rejects differently."* I re-derived that chain on `origin/main` myself instead of taking the PR body's word:

- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-activity.object.ts:57` — `type: Field.select([…11 values…], { required: true, readonly: true, … })`; `scheduled` genuinely absent ⇒ premise true at review time
- `packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts:1023` (insert) and `:1033` (update) — both `if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;`, and both sit **above** the `validateOne` call
- `validateOne` is declared at `:475`; every `invalid_option` failure is inside it (`:659`, `:680`, `:682`)

Lines `:276` and `:655` also matched `invalid_option` — both prose comments, read and discarded rather than counted. ⇒ The chain holds: a readonly select field's declared options are unreachable, so adding one changes no behaviour.

The PR's own measurement is the better half of this and is worth naming: with the enum value added and nothing else changed, **exactly one of 313 assertions moved**, and it was the declarative census pin — while `activity-type-vocabulary-enforcement.test.ts`, which inserts an *undeclared* value into this very column and asserts it lands, stayed **green in the same run**. That observes the mechanism from both sides. A change that only the literal inventory can see, and that the behavioural suite cannot, is exactly what "documentation catching up to reality" should look like.

### Docs Drift Check — verified, no drift

The advisory listed three hand-written pages naming `sys_activity`. That check is **symbol-anchored and precision-first (#9192)**, so it flags a page for naming the symbol — it cannot see whether the page makes a *prose* claim this diff falsifies. Checked by hand:

| page | enumerates `sys_activity.type` values? |
|---|---|
| `kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx` | **no** — its `'login' \| 'logout'` at `:31` is `recordAuthEvent`'s `action` on **`sys_audit_log`**, a different object |
| `plugins/packages.mdx` | no |
| `ui/setup-app.mdx` | no |

Positive control run first, so the zero-hit is a real absence and not a broken query: all five flagged files do contain `sys_activity` (1–3 occurrences each), which is precisely why the anchor listed them. **No page needs updating.**

The two release-owned pages (`releases/v14.mdx`, `releases/v16.mdx`) were **read only** and neither enumerates the vocabulary. Correctly untouched — release notes are written centrally at release time.

### Scope beyond direction 1 — reviewed and accepted

Three things go past the literal one-line ask, all named openly in the PR body rather than left to be found:

1. the second `TYPES_WITH_WRITERS` writer for `completed` — documentation, no assertion change
2. two stale docblock sentences (the hardcoded `"eleven-value"` count dropped so it cannot rot again; the objectui set-equality claim past-tensed to the #8203 census and attributed to objectui#5840, marked **not measured here**)
3. the four regenerated locale bundles — a consequence of the enum change, not scope creep

All documentation, all in a file the card already required editing, and **none settles the closed-vs-open vocabulary question**. The `documentation, not a contract` phrasing in the docblock was already there and is untouched. Accepted.

### Landing

`Part of #11424`, not `Fixes` — the corresponding gate passed, so merging closes nothing and directions 2/3/4 survive on #11424 and #11507.

Clause-② **no**: no `packages/spec/**` path, and no accept/reject change (verified above). This is inside seat discretion. **Merge queue only, never bypassed.** Flipping ready once `Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3)` — the last job still running — reports green.

⭐ The third door this PR's investigation surfaced (an app action writing this column directly through `ctx.api`, invisible to any grep of this repo) is recorded on **#11507**, where it corrects the *scope* of the pending vocabulary ruling. Nothing here rules on it.
